newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish MPs pass first reading of banking law.
newsitem.headline: Polish MPs pass first reading of banking law.

text.p: gave initial approval to a draft banking law, designed to enhance security and bring the banking system in line with EU standards, and sent it to committees for further work.

The bill, which passed its first reading in the lower house, would provide for an independent Banking Supervision Commission that would oversee the sector and guard against unfair competition between banks.

The bill aims to regulate more closely the origins of banks' capital and their ownership structures, preventing the dangerous expansion of so-called internal loans and helping to protect against money laundering.

The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank which helped draft the bill, says it would make banks safer for Poles and help accumulate savings deposits, which would in future be used to finance the country's economic growth.

Among the bill's provisions is a ban on banks tying up more than 15 percent of own funds to buy shares of companies that that are not banks, but they will be allowed to extend credits worth up to 25 percent of own funds to a single entity.

Any purchaser of a bank's shares representing five percent or more of votes at its shareholders' meeting will have to report the move to the new Banking Supervision Commission, which must also give its agreement for purchases taking voting powers across further successive thresholds.

Last month Finance Minister Marek Belka said he hoped legislators would pass the bill before general elections due around September, otherwise a new government and parliament might start work afresh, further delaying its passage.

Earlier NBP President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz accused the government of neglecting the banking bill and of being concerned only about a new central bank charter, which would give it powers to decide who would sit on some policy-making boards.
